Twelve selected/unselected scalar and two-cell record machine-code cases pass on Windows and Debian with identical 3633-byte code. The current-source native lowering regression owner passes 37 cases on each host.

limitations: Native WVB 1.39 module admission remains closed. Machine-code snippet execution does not establish full candidate-module execution, lifetime safety, authority preservation, cleanup or real-consumer integration.

The probe invokes the maintained data/type fixture, including 80 owner/view/projection combinations and structural emission/storage checks. Its 12 machine cases cover scalar and two-cell record payloads only; descriptor and owned-payload execution are not qualified.

E1 snapshots selected payload cells without acquiring ownership. The complete caller-side lifetime proof and native borrowed call/value/cleanup integration remain pending before admission can open. Owner-local use tracking at E1 is not proof of retention for the entire loan.
Unselected cases preserve sentinel payload storage; structural checks verify the branch skips payload instructions. No guard-page unreadable-owner-payload test was run.

Passing construction uses existing development caches keyed by source and tool inputs. This is not independent clean bootstrap reconstruction. Raw machine probes were temporary and removed by the existing owner.

PlanOnly selected seed and native-x64-lowering-development, editor checks and a managed-test-recovery-source gap. The causal existing native owner and routing verifier were selected directly. Full native development, compiler reconstruction, frozen compiler qualification, browser, editor and installed-tool gates were not run because this checkpoint does not change their claimed surface.
Exclusive borrow, Take/Map, maintained package consumer migration and the full compiler/libraries goal remain pending.
